subject: Request: subprocessor jurisdictions & export controls for renewal
messages:
From: Elena Burke <elena.burke@alphafin.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Subprocessor origin & export controls for upcoming renewal

Hi Rishi,

Quick note as we start the contract renewal run for our AI platform integration: Legal and Procurement need a current list of Redwood subprocessors plus the primary data residency/jurisdiction where each subprocesses customer identifiable content. Specifically we need: 

- Full roster of subprocessors in scope for API/telemetry/observability/metrics
- Country of processing and whether data may cross borders (yes/no)
- Any onshore fallback or EU/UK-specific onshore routing options
- Whether key management or logs are handled by a 3rd party and where the KMS/HSM is located

Can you provide a CSV or a short export and a schematic of transit flows? AlphaFin has an internal export control checklist that flags vendors that process PII outside the US for additional review — we want to close that loop before renewal.

If you can send the roster and an expected evidence delivery date we can triage on our side.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Burke
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Alpha Financial Services
[attachment: none]

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up.

We can do that. Quick clarifications so we return what you need:

- You want the roster for all subprocessors that touch customer request payloads, observability telemetry, and metadata (yes/no)?
- Is a single CSV with columns (vendor, role, country_of_processing, crossborder_allowed, kms_location, sla_notes) sufficient?
- For transit flows, would a 1-page PDF diagram showing the primary routes (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private) work, or do you need a per-tenant map?

Internal note to Kimberly / Marissa: please pull the canonical subprocessor export (latest inventory) and the transit map. Flag any vendors with EU processing for explicit onshore options.

We aim to deliver a first-pass package tomorrow EOD PST and can follow with supporting certificates (SCCs/SCC addendum references) early next week.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Trust & Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the quick reply. The CSV template you proposed looks good. Two quick asks: 

1) If any subprocessors perform ephemeral caching or edge-processing inside jurisdictions outside the US, please mark the row with "transient" in the crossborder_allowed column and add a short note on duration (e.g., minutes/hours).
2) For any KMS/HSM usage, include the operator contact (vendor support alias) so we can route KMS attestation questions directly.

I'm attaching the procurement checklist and a sample CSV we use for other vendors — it might help with column names.

We'll need the roster + transit map by EOD your local time tomorrow to stay on our renewal schedule. If that's not possible, please provide a prioritized subset (top 10 vendors by footprint) and ETA for the rest.

Best,

Elena — attaching our export and a simplified transit map. See notes below for edge cases and next steps.

Attachments: alpha_subprocessors_20271130.csv; data_transfer_map_v2.pdf

Key notes (summary):
- CSV includes vendor, role, primary_country, crossborder_flag (no / transient / yes), transient_duration, kms_location, support_contact, notes
- We flagged three vendors as "transient" where brief edge caching may occur in the EU (typically minutes, rare spikes). Those rows include estimated durations and TTL.
- KMS/HSM: primary key management is with Redwood KMS (on-prem HSM for Dedicated customers). For hosted customers some envelope keys are managed by our cloud KMS providers — see kms_location column. Support aliases are included.
- Evidence: for any vendor rows where you require attestations we can produce export logs, SCC references and a vendor-signed encryption attestation PDF. Expect those in 3 business days for priority vendors.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm which vendors you want attestations for (reply with vendor names + items requested).
2) If AlphaFin needs onshore-only routing for specific tenants, share tenant IDs and region constraints; we'll scope a routing addendum and timeline.
3) I'll loop legal for a DPA amendment if any new onshore routing or dedicated KMS requirements are requested.

If that timeline works I'll create a HubSpot ticket (HS-324918) and a DocuSign envelope for any DPA addendums.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Trust & Security Operations
